Selecting an audio clip exposes Slice and Convert Harmony/Melody/Drums commands in Create or clip context menu. Multi-selection, frozen/group/return/video/take-lane and unsupported source eligibility remain U.

Slice opens a dialog with beat-resolution, transient or Warp Marker divisions and slicing-preset selection. Slicing partitions source time rather than recognizing pitch. Exact division counting, first/last markers and boundary rounding remain U.

The slicing workflow prevents proceeding when the chosen plan would exceed128 slices; lower resolution or smaller selected region can reduce the count. This is the slicing-command limit, not a blanket cap on arbitrary rack chains. Exact counting and other eligibility errors remain U.

Slicing presets include supplied templates and user templates from the User Library Defaults folder. Preserve warped timing retains Warp timing changes; disabled follows raw source timing instead. Exact field/default precedence, resampling, fades and audio equality remain U.

On successful Slice confirmation a new MIDI track contains a MIDI clip with one chromatically ordered note per slice and a Drum Rack with one chain/Simpler per slice. Each chain responds to its corresponding note and loads the corresponding source region. Starting pitch, note lengths/velocities, media copying and exact reference/boundary representation remain U.

Mappings come from the chosen slicing preset; supplied examples include envelope/loop/crossfade controls. A mapped macro adjusts corresponding parameters across the Simplers. Playback triggers slices in original sequence and selected/source timing; exact sample equivalence and processing duration remain U.

Editing slice notes or swapping rack pad note mappings can reorder playback. Per-chain effects process individual slices; selected chains can be grouped into a nested rack and effects placed after it for shared processing. Generic note/rack operations remain owned by their existing contracts.

Harmony extracts pitched polyphonic content into a new MIDI track/clip with a piano-sound Instrument Rack. It is note recognition and resynthesis, not playback of the original waveform. Exact detected pitches/times/velocities, polyphony and default preset identity are U.

Melody targets monophonic pitched audio, creating a new MIDI track/clip with a synthesizer Instrument Rack. Its Synth to Piano macro spans analog-style synth/electric-piano character. Exact detection, macro mapping and preset/DSP identity remain U.

Drums extracts unpitched percussive rhythm into a new MIDI track/clip and preloaded Drum Rack, attempting kick/snare/hihat classification. No perfect classifier or exact MIDI key/sample/velocity assignment is promised.

Convert uses source transients for note divisions; changing those markers can alter conversion. Clear isolated attacks and uncompressed audio are recommendations, not guaranteed detection. Wrong-source-class conversion may add notes; reconstruction/precision/recall, onset tie, polyphony and lossy-codec effects remain U.

Pitch/onset/classifier thresholds, tuning/reference pitch, amplitude-to-velocity, overlap/length, silent/ambiguous/invalid source behavior and deterministic repeatability have no finite target oracle here. Retained native task names do not supply a full recognition contract.

Tempo/meter/warp/loop/region/selection changes during processing, source preservation, routing/monitoring, launch ownership, undo grouping, error or cancellation and result placement have no complete oracle.

Save/reopen, sample copy/collect, missing files, malformed audio/preset, CPU/memory/disk failure, cancellation at progress boundaries and device/Set/application teardown require exact outcomes beyond normal documented creation.
